borders: Trapsoul stays under Trap: the drums are trap, so the tag is not R&B.
Rage stays its own parent. It is the Carti/Yeat scene, not a dark-trap preset.
Premier, Pete Rock, RZA, and Mobb Deep are Boom Bap. The word 90s, with no such producer, is the 90s parent. In this catalog that word means 90s hip-hop, not pop.
Cumbia is Latin, not Dancehall. Reggaeton stays Caribbean because it is the dembow riddim family, not Latin pop.
Afroswing stays under UK. It is a London fusion (J Hus, NSG, Not3s, Kojo Funds): afrobeats drums plus dancehall plus UK road rap. The type-beat market is British.
Phonk on the 2010s parent is original and drift phonk. Brazilian Phonk stays under Latin.
Jazz sits under Lo-fi and is not its own radio button. Country and 80s stay on the map even when they have no main button.

parents.name: Trap
parents.definition: 808s, rolling hats, and a loop built for a rap verse. The parent plays every trap subgenre.
parents.differs: Drill slides the 808. Rage is the distorted opium scene and stays its own parent. Plugg uses the sparse plugg drum, not this hat roll.

subgenres.name: Trap
subgenres.definition: A straight trap type beat: hat rolls and 808s with no tighter tag. Matches trap type beat and type beat trap. Trap metal type beat lands here too.
subgenres.differs: Melodic trap has a sung or guitar hook. Hoodtrap and supertrap are the named tags. Dark Trap is the horror preset. Generic trap is what is left.

subgenres.name: Melodic Trap
subgenres.definition: Trap drums under a guitar line or a sung melody. The melody is the hook, not a garnish.
subgenres.differs: Generic trap can be drums and a loop with no lead melody. Juice WRLD stays here unless the title says emo, which moves him to Emo Rap.

subgenres.name: Dark/Aggressive
subgenres.label: Dark Trap
subgenres.definition: The existing dark-trap string, labeled Dark Trap: horror-score stabs or a harsher trap mix. Rows keep the name Dark/Aggressive.
subgenres.differs: Rage is a separate parent with opium drums. Drift phonk is the 2010s Phonk tag, not this preset.

subgenres.name: Trapsoul
subgenres.definition: Trap drums under R&B chords and a sung pocket. The title has to say trapsoul or trap soul.
subgenres.differs: Trapsoul is under Trap, not R&B. R&B is the sung record without the trap-drum tag. Bryson Tiller stays R&B unless the title says trapsoul.

subgenres.name: Hoodtrap
subgenres.definition: The hoodtrap tag: a grimy trap loop producers already file under trap.
subgenres.differs: It is trap, not a different genre. Supertrap is the other named tag. Afrotrap is not this pattern and stays untagged.

subgenres.name: Supertrap
subgenres.definition: The supertrap tag: the brighter internet trap offshoot, still trap drums.
subgenres.differs: Hoodtrap is the grimier tag. Generic trap is trap type beat without the supertrap word.

subgenres.name: Detroit
subgenres.definition: Detroit rap pocket: off-beat flows and the minor-key loops Babytron, Veeze, and 42 Dugg beats copy.
subgenres.differs: Generic trap does not have the Detroit pocket. Midwest, the hip-hop region tag, is under Rap.

parents.name: Rage
parents.definition: Distorted opium drums and the Carti/Yeat lane. Its own parent, not a trap preset.
parents.differs: Dark Trap is a horror trap mix under Trap. Lil Uzi Vert lands here only when the title says rage, not when it says emo or soundcloud.

subgenres.name: Rage/Opium
subgenres.definition: The rage and opium string. Carti, Yeat, and the opium drum kit.
subgenres.differs: A dark trap preset with no rage or opium word stays Dark Trap. Uzi with rage in the title is this, not Emo Rap.

parents.name: Drill
parents.definition: Sliding 808s. NY drill and UK drill are the same string.
parents.differs: UK drill stays on this button. The UK parent does not steal it. Trap hats do not slide.

subgenres.name: Drill
subgenres.definition: Drill, including uk drill and ny drill. One database string.
subgenres.differs: There is no second drill genre. A UK rap title with no drill word stays UK Rap.

parents.name: 2010s
parents.definition: 2010s internet rap that is not trap, rage, or drill: plugg, emo rap, and original phonk.
parents.differs: Brazilian Phonk is Latin. Melodic trap stays under Trap. Rage stays its own parent.

subgenres.name: Plugg/Pluggnb
subgenres.definition: The plugg and pluggnb string: sparse drums, the Pierre Bourne and MexikoDro pocket.
subgenres.differs: Generic trap has rolling hats. Plugg is the thinner internet drum. The old Plugg-only button is this subgenre now.

subgenres.name: Emo Rap
subgenres.definition: Soundcloud-era emo rap. Lil Peep, XXXTentacion, and Lil Tracy map here.
subgenres.differs: Lil Uzi Vert is Emo Rap only when the title says emo or soundcloud, and not when it says rage. Juice WRLD stays Melodic Trap unless the title says emo. Midwest emo is Alt.

subgenres.name: Phonk
subgenres.definition: Original phonk and drift phonk. Memphis-derived cowbell loops and the later drift edit.
subgenres.differs: Brazilian phonk and funk phonk are Brazilian Phonk under Latin. A bare phonk title is this, not that.

parents.name: Boom Bap
parents.definition: Boom-bap practice and the east-coast lineage: chopped breaks, not a coast-less hip-hop loop.
parents.differs: The Rap button is for hip-hop that names no coast and no boom-bap practice. The word 90s is the 90s parent, even when the beat is also boom bap.

subgenres.name: Boom Bap/Old School
subgenres.definition: Boom bap and old school. Premier, Pete Rock, RZA, Mobb Deep, and Nas.
subgenres.differs: A title that says 90s is the 90s parent. These producer names without that word stay here. Jay-Z alone stays untagged.

subgenres.name: East Coast
subgenres.definition: The east-coast tag when the title names the coast and no tighter boom-bap or drill phrase.
subgenres.differs: Do not file this under Rap. Drill with an east-coast city still wins as Drill when the title says drill.

subgenres.name: Conscious
subgenres.definition: Conscious rap. Little Simz maps here.
subgenres.differs: A generic hip-hop title with no conscious word is the Hip-Hop string under Rap. Smino is Hip-Hop, not this.

parents.name: West Coast
parents.definition: West-coast rap and g-funk. The coast is the parent, not a leftover hip-hop tag.
parents.differs: G-funk is the whining synth under this parent. It does not go on the Rap button.

subgenres.name: West Coast
subgenres.definition: The west-coast tag. 2Pac stays here rather than on 90s.
subgenres.differs: G-Funk is the tighter Dre synth tag. A 90s word still goes to the 90s parent.

subgenres.name: G-Funk
subgenres.definition: G-funk. The high synth and the Dre pocket.
subgenres.differs: Dr. Dre stays G-Funk, not generic West Coast and not 90s. A west-coast title with no g-funk word stays West Coast.

parents.name: Southern
parents.definition: Southern rap that is not trap and not the crunk chant.
parents.differs: Trap is its own parent. Crunk is the subgenre under this one, not a separate button.

subgenres.name: Southern
subgenres.definition: The southern and dirty-south tag.
subgenres.differs: Crunk is the chant record. Trap drums from Atlanta stay Trap, not Southern.

subgenres.name: Crunk
subgenres.definition: Crunk. The chant and the Three 6 / Lil Jon pocket.
subgenres.differs: Southern without the crunk word stays Southern. Trap is not crunk.

parents.name: Rap
parents.definition: Beats that say hip-hop but name no coast and no boom-bap practice.
parents.differs: East Coast stays Boom Bap. G-Funk stays West Coast. Do not dump either into this button.

subgenres.name: Hip-Hop
subgenres.definition: The generic leftover hip-hop string. Drake, Doechii, and Smino.
subgenres.differs: If the title names a coast, boom bap, trap, or drill, that tighter tag wins. This is what is left.

subgenres.name: Midwest
subgenres.definition: The midwest hip-hop region tag.
subgenres.differs: Midwest emo is Alt. The word midwest alone is this region, not the emo guitar tag.

subgenres.name: Pop Rap
subgenres.definition: Pop rap. The title says pop rap.
subgenres.differs: Pop country is Country. A melodic trap guitar is Melodic Trap, not pop rap.

parents.name: R&B
parents.definition: Sung R&B, classic soul, psychedelic soul, and funk.
parents.differs: Trapsoul is Trap. Dance pop is Club. The word 80s is the 80s parent, not a reason to move Prince here.

subgenres.name: R&B
subgenres.definition: R&B. The Weeknd, Erykah Badu, Frank Ocean, Rihanna, and Hamza.
subgenres.differs: Trapsoul needs the trapsoul words and lives under Trap. Bryson Tiller stays R&B unless the title says trapsoul.

subgenres.name: Classic Soul
subgenres.definition: Classic soul. The title says classic soul.
subgenres.differs: A modern R&B title with no classic-soul words stays R&B.

subgenres.name: Psychedelic Soul
subgenres.definition: Psychedelic soul. The title says psychedelic soul.
subgenres.differs: Prince without that phrase is not pulled off his existing tag, and a title that says 80s is the 80s parent.

subgenres.name: Funk
subgenres.definition: Funk as the American band pocket, not Brazilian funk.
subgenres.differs: Brazilian funk and baile funk are Latin. G-funk is West Coast. This string is the funk tag under R&B.

parents.name: UK
parents.definition: UK rap, grime, UK garage, road rap, and afroswing.
parents.differs: UK drill is Drill, not this parent. Afrobeats is Afro. Afroswing stays here.

subgenres.name: UK Rap
subgenres.definition: UK rap. Dave, Nines, Potter Payper, Marnz Malone, Clavish, D Block Europe, Bugzy Malone, Knucks, Nemzzz, Unknown T, Loyle Carner.
subgenres.differs: Headie One and Central Cee are Drill. Grime is its own string. Dave is the exact token, not every Dave.

subgenres.name: Grime
subgenres.definition: Grime. Dizzee Rascal and Giggs.
subgenres.differs: UK rap without the grime word stays UK Rap. UK drill is Drill.

subgenres.name: UK Garage
subgenres.definition: UK garage, 2-step, and speed garage.
subgenres.differs: Jersey club is Club. Amapiano is Afro. This is the UK garage shuffle.

subgenres.name: Road Rap
subgenres.definition: Road rap. The title says road rap.
subgenres.differs: UK rap is the wider string. Drill is the sliding 808, even from London.

subgenres.name: Afroswing
subgenres.definition: Afroswing is a London fusion: J Hus, NSG, Not3s, and Kojo Funds. Afrobeats drums plus dancehall plus UK road rap. The type-beat market is British, so the tag stays under UK.
subgenres.differs: It is not Afrobeats, not Dancehall, and not Caribbean. Those are the ingredients. The buyers are looking for a UK beat.

parents.name: Afro
parents.definition: Afrobeats and the West African family: classic afrobeat, afropop, afrofusion, amapiano, highlife.
parents.differs: Afroswing stays under UK. Afrotrap is not a trap subgenre and stays untagged.

subgenres.name: Afrobeat (Classic)
subgenres.definition: Classic afrobeat. The long Fela pocket, not the pop afrobeats drum.
subgenres.differs: Afropop and amapiano are the newer strings. Afroswing is UK.

subgenres.name: Afropop
subgenres.definition: Afropop and afro pop.
subgenres.differs: Amapiano has the log drum. Classic afrobeat is the older big-band form.

subgenres.name: Afrofusion
subgenres.definition: Afrofusion and afro fusion.
subgenres.differs: A named amapiano or afropop title beats this wider word.

subgenres.name: Amapiano-Afrobeats
subgenres.definition: Amapiano and the 3-step / amapiano-afrobeats pocket. Jazzworx and Dlala Thukzin.
subgenres.differs: UK garage is a different shuffle. Jazz under Lo-fi is not this, even though Jazzworx has jazz in the name.

subgenres.name: Highlife
subgenres.definition: Highlife. The title says highlife.
subgenres.differs: Afropop is the wider pop string. Highlife needs the word.

parents.name: Caribbean
parents.definition: Dancehall, dembow, and reggaeton. The dembow riddim family.
parents.differs: Reggaeton stays here because of the dembow, not because it is Latin pop. Cumbia, Brazilian funk, and corridos are Latin. Afroswing is UK.

subgenres.name: Dancehall
subgenres.definition: Dancehall. Existing dancehall rows stay dancehall.
subgenres.differs: Dembow and reggaeton are their own strings. Roots reggae and ragga are not on this parent.

subgenres.name: Dembow
subgenres.definition: Dembow. El Alfa.
subgenres.differs: Reggaeton is the wider commercial dembow song. A title that says dembow is this string.

subgenres.name: Reggaeton
subgenres.definition: Reggaeton. Blessd and Lomiiel. It stays Caribbean because it is the dembow riddim family.
subgenres.differs: Latin trap uses trap hats, not this dembow. Cumbia is Latin. RKT is the Argentine club edit, also Latin.

parents.name: Latin
parents.definition: Latin beats that are not the Caribbean dembow family: cumbia, Brazilian funk, Brazilian phonk, corridos tumbados, latin trap, and RKT.
parents.differs: Dancehall, dembow, and reggaeton are Caribbean. Drift phonk is 2010s. Bare funk is not Brazilian funk.

subgenres.name: Cumbia
subgenres.definition: Cumbia. Its own string.
subgenres.differs: Not folded into dancehall. RKT is the Argentine club edit of cumbia villera, not this plain cumbia tag.

subgenres.name: Brazilian Funk
subgenres.definition: Brazilian funk, baile funk, and funk carioca.
subgenres.differs: The word funk alone is not this. Funk under R&B is the American pocket. Jersey club is not baile funk.

subgenres.name: Brazilian Phonk
subgenres.definition: Brazilian phonk and funk phonk only.
subgenres.differs: A bare phonk title is Phonk under 2010s. This tag needs brazilian phonk or funk phonk.

subgenres.name: Corridos Tumbados
subgenres.definition: Corridos tumbados. Requinto or sierreño guitar with a tuba or an 808, the tumbado pocket.
subgenres.differs: Not reggaeton and not cumbia. Gera MX, Aleman, and Makabelico belong to this string.

subgenres.name: Latin Trap
subgenres.definition: Latin trap. Trap hats with a Spanish-language hook. The title says latin trap.
subgenres.differs: English trap type beat stays Trap. Reggaeton is dembow, not these hats.

subgenres.name: RKT
subgenres.definition: RKT. Argentine cumbia villera pushed with a club kick. L-Gante is the reference.
subgenres.differs: Not reggaeton, even though the drums borrow from it. Not plain cumbia, and not Brazilian funk.

parents.name: Club
parents.definition: House, deep house, EDM club bangers, jersey club, and dance pop.
parents.differs: There is no Deep House station. Jersey club is its own string under this parent.

subgenres.name: Club
subgenres.definition: Deep house, house, the word club, edm, and club banger.
subgenres.differs: Jersey Club and Dance Pop are the other strings. A strip-club title is not the house tag.

subgenres.name: Jersey Club
subgenres.definition: Jersey club. The bed squeak and the jersey kick pattern.
subgenres.differs: A house loop or an EDM club banger is Club, not jersey. Baile funk is Brazilian Funk.

subgenres.name: Dance Pop
subgenres.definition: Dance pop. The title says dance pop.
subgenres.differs: R&B is the sung ballad pocket. The word 80s is the 80s parent, not dance pop, unless the title also says dance pop.

parents.name: Alt
parents.definition: Guitars that are not country: alternative rock, indie rock, grunge, shoegaze, midwest emo, and Nirvana.
parents.differs: When a title names several, the order is shoegaze, then grunge, then Nirvana, then midwest emo, then indie rock, then alternative rock.

subgenres.name: Alternative Rock
subgenres.definition: Alternative rock or alt rock.
subgenres.differs: It loses to shoegaze, grunge, Nirvana, midwest emo, and indie rock when those are also named.

subgenres.name: Indie Rock
subgenres.definition: Indie rock, or indie sitting next to rock or alternative.
subgenres.differs: The word indie alone is not enough. Alternative rock with no indie is Alternative Rock.

subgenres.name: Grunge
subgenres.definition: Grunge. The title says grunge.
subgenres.differs: Nirvana is its own string when the title names the band. Shoegaze beats grunge when both are named.

subgenres.name: Shoegaze
subgenres.definition: Shoegaze and shoegazing. Washed guitars.
subgenres.differs: It beats grunge and the other rock tags when both are named.

subgenres.name: Midwest Emo
subgenres.definition: Midwest emo, including a sad midwest emo acoustic title.
subgenres.differs: Midwest rap is under Rap. Emo rap is the 2010s soundcloud tag. This tag needs the words midwest emo.

subgenres.name: Nirvana
subgenres.definition: A Nirvana type beat. The band name.
subgenres.differs: Grunge without the name Nirvana stays Grunge. Nirvana beats midwest emo and indie rock.

parents.name: Lo-fi
parents.definition: Lo-fi, chill, and jazz. Jazz is a subgenre here, not its own radio button. The map can still select Jazz alone.
parents.differs: A jazz sample inside boom bap, with no jazz word, stays Boom Bap. Country guitar is Country.

subgenres.name: Lo-fi/Chill
subgenres.definition: Lo-fi, lofi, chill, and chillhop as one genre string.
subgenres.differs: A title that says jazz or jazzy is Jazz, the other subgenre on this parent.

subgenres.name: Jazz
subgenres.definition: Jazz and jazzy beats. Selectable on its own from this map.
subgenres.differs: Lo-fi can be dusty without being jazz. Boom bap can sample jazz without the word. This tag needs jazz or jazzy.

parents.name: 90s
parents.definition: The word 90s. In this catalog that is 90s hip-hop: boom bap, Memphis, and west-coast gangsta, not Britney or Backstreet pop.
parents.differs: DJ Premier, Pete Rock, RZA, and Mobb Deep without the word 90s stay Boom Bap. Jay-Z alone stays untagged.

subgenres.name: 90s
subgenres.definition: The 90s word as its own subgenre. Same reading as the parent: 90s hip-hop.
subgenres.differs: A boom-bap producer name with no 90s word is Boom Bap, not this.

parents.name: 2000s
parents.definition: The word 2000s, plus the producers beatmakers still name for that pocket. In this catalog that is 2000s hip-hop and R&B production, not 2000s pop.
parents.differs: A few titles are indie or nu-metal. The pile is Neptunes, Pharrell, and Timbaland. Not Premier, Pete Rock, RZA, or Mobb Deep.

subgenres.name: 2000s
subgenres.definition: The 2000s word, and those producer names when the title names them.
subgenres.differs: Boom-bap names stay Boom Bap. Dr. Dre stays G-Funk.

parents.name: 80s
parents.definition: The word 80s. In this catalog that is synth, funk, city pop, and pop more often than 80s rap. No main radio button while the pile is thin. The bubble stays, and the tag stays searchable.
parents.differs: Prince or Michael Jackson without the word 80s is not pulled here. A title that says 80s is this subgenre even when it is not a station button.

subgenres.name: 80s
subgenres.definition: The 80s word: synth pop, synthwave, funk, and city pop in the titles that carry it.
subgenres.differs: It is not an 80s-rap button. The sample is Take On Me, city pop, and synth pop, with only a few rap records using an 80s sample.

parents.name: Country
parents.definition: Country type beat and country folk, including country rap. No main radio button while the pile is under about 5,000. The parent is still Country, and the bubble stays searchable.
parents.differs: Alt is the rock guitar family. A Zach Bryan or Dylan Gossett title is this, not indie rock.

subgenres.name: Country
subgenres.definition: Country, country folk, and country rap.
subgenres.differs: Not a midwest emo acoustic title unless the word country is there.

parents.name: Meme
parents.definition: High-signal joke and brainrot subjects only.
parents.differs: Not a producer name and not a band that only shares a noun. Cigarettes After Sex is not Meme. Rizzy is not Meme.

subgenres.name: Meme
subgenres.definition: 500 cigarettes, skibidi, trollge, meme cockroach, among us, goofy ahh, subway surfers, rat dance, shrek type beat, smurf cat, deez nuts, meme rap, meme type beat.
subgenres.differs: Bare cigarette or cigarettes is not enough. The 500 cigarettes meme is the phrase. A trap drum under skibidi is still Meme.

parents.name: Underground
parents.definition: Still untagged. The UG MIX button.
parents.differs: Anything with a parent has left this pile. Ambient, experimental, ragga, and roots reggae have no parent, so they are not bubbles and they are not buttons.

subgenres.name: Underground
subgenres.definition: No subgenre yet.
subgenres.differs: Not a style. It is the remainder.
